text:
maya: Heads-up: scheduling a short maintenance window for pool-saturn next Mon 02:00-03:00 UTC. We need to perform a soft quarantine + controlled reboot sweep on 8 racks to mitigate recent thermal-throttle spikes. Expect rolling reboots with live eviction, ~10 racks/minute cadence.

tom: ETA on user-facing impact? will hosted API routes be affected?

maya: No full outage expected. We'll cordon nodes via autoscaler policies, drain tasks with graceful 60s timeout, warm cache afterwards. Some tail latencies could increase for 5-10m for affected tenants.

lina: Can we run a canary on one rack first and validate KV cache seeding? who owns the canary check?

harry: I'll run canary. Plan: cordon rack-a3, reboot, run perf-check (3 queries at p95 target), then uncordon. If perf ok, proceed.

maya: Great. Please follow the rollback checklist if p95 > 2x baseline or error rate +20%.

sre-bot: Calendar event created: "saturn maintenance - thermal mitigation" Mon 02:00 UTC. Notifying @oncall and @platform-eng.

tom: Do we have capacity headroom in eu-west2 if we need to divert? cost implications?

maya: Yes, we have ~12% spare in eu-west2 and ~8% in us-west1. If we fail canary, we'll route traffic to eu-west2 and pause further reboots. Cost hit estimated ~$1.2k/hr in burst pricing for the diversion window.

lina: Can we pre-warm prefix cache to reduce regen load?

harry: Plan includes KV seed script after each rack reboot. Running:
```bash
# seed cache with popular prefixes
./tools/kv-seed --pool saturn --prefix-file infra/cache-top1000.txt --concurrency 6
```
Will monitor seeding progress in prometheus: infra.kv.seed.rate and runtime.token.latency_p95.

maya: Runbook excerpt for ops:
1) Run canary on rack-a3.
2) If canary OK -> schedule cohort of 2 racks every 10m.
3) If canary FAIL -> stop, failover traffic to eu-west2, open incident, rollback any partial reboots.
4) Post-maint: run synthetic smoke suites and sanity checks for 30m.

tom: How are we handling dedicated customers pinned to those racks? any manual migrations?

maya: Dedicated customers on saturn are on different tenant pools; only 2 tenants overlap with our target racks. We'll manually migrate their jobs to reserved nodes before we start. Solutions team notified.

lina: Add a fallback policy to route to smaller-quantized variant if capacity dips unexpectedly.

harry: Done. Also toggled automatic fallback in routing for saturn -> quantized-v2.

maya: Logging note: preserve node logs and nvme SMART output to /var/log/maint/saturn-1745109876/ for later telemetry analysis.

sre-bot: Reminder: Escalation policy for this window is the usual chain: oncall -> eng-lead -> infra-ops.

tom: I'll stand by during the window and watch latency dashboards. :eyes:

maya: Thanks. If any red flags during canary we abort and notify customers. Otherwise expect all racks back by 03:05 UTC. :thumbsup:
